exposure: Mode of delivery (Caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Hospitalization for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection
cohort: All children born in Denmark between January 1997 and June 2003
finding: Delivery by caesarean section is associated with an increased risk of hospitalization for RSV infection, with the effect persisting for at least the first 2 years of life.
mod_finding: Both acute and elective caesarean sections were associated with an increased risk of hospitalization for RSV infection compared to vaginal delivery.
